title: Cobalt Dynamics - Pilot security gates, benchmarks & load criteria
summary: POC scoping focused on security gates (SOC 2 / ISO / SSO), audit log retention, SAML + SCIM integration, RBAC model, and performance acceptance criteria. Agreed on a 4-week pilot with specific benchmark targets and a security review milestone. Next steps: share SOC 2/ISO docs, SSO integration playbook, test dataset, and preliminary pricing. Action items assigned for benchmark plan and SSO test account.
topics: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 requirements
SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning and RBAC mapping
Workload sizing: qps, concurrency, token lengths
Benchmarks: latency targets and throughput (95th pct)

Aisha: provide sample production logs and token size distribution — due 2026-04-30
Jordan: share SOC2 / ISO artifacts and Redwood security datasheet link — due 2026-04-29
Priyanka: confirm required audit log retention period (legal) and any export format constraints — due 2026-05-03
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC 2 Type II attestation + ISO 27001 summary and security playbook
Provision SSO test tenant (SAML) and share SCIM mapping template

transcript:
Meeting: Cobalt Dynamics - Pilot security gates, benchmarks & load criteria
Date: 2026-04-28 15:00 PDT | Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Jordan B. (Redwood AE); Samira C. (Redwood SE); Michael T. (Cobalt Head of Platform); Aisha R. (DevOps); Priyanka S. (Security Lead); Leo P. (PM)

Summary Notes: quick run through of compliance asks, then technical scoping for the load/benchmark side. Clear ask for SOC 2 + ISO artifacts, SAML/SCIM integration, RBAC mapping and audit log retention. Agreed acceptance criteria for performance and security gates.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're excited to scope this pilot with Cobalt Dynamics. Samira and I will take the technical bits; Jordan short intro — we're Redwood Inference, we run hosted/dedicated/private inference, uh mostly focused on production economics.
[00:22] Michael: yep thanks. Quick background: we're building an internal summon assistant for ops and we need to make sure data governance is solid — security is a hard stop for us.
[00:32] Samira: totally, that's the right place to start. Priyanka — can you give us the must-have compliance gates for the pilot?
[00:38] Priyanka: sure. From a security perspective, we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, an ISO 27001 attestation if available, SSO via SAML with SCIM provisioning, RBAC that maps to our groups, and audit logs with at least 12 months retention. Also encryption at rest keys via our KMS preferred (HSM is fine).
[01:02] Jordan: OK great. We have SOC 2 Type II and an ISO summary — we'll send the artifact. For SSO we support SAML and SCIM; we can do group mapping for RBAC. Audit logs are available via console and exportable. We'll share formats.
[01:18] Priyanka: how granular are your audit logs? I need user, token, model id, request, and raw response hashes, timestamps, and admin actions.
[01:26] Samira: our logs include request/response metadata and action logs; the raw prompt may be masked optionally. We can include model variant, token counts, latencies, and an opaque request id. Full response hashes can be generated. There's sometimes some small differences in field names — we can provide a sample CSV/JSON export.
[01:49] Aisha: for the pilot we also need to test SAML provisioning. We use Okta and Azure AD; can you confirm SCIM supported attributes?
[01:57] Samira: yes Okta + AAD supported. SCIM mapping typically includes email, displayName, groups. We'll send a mapping template. Note: occasionally SCIM provisioning rate-limits require a short warm-up but works.
[02:18] Leo: on the performance side, our baseline is current in-house service with median latency around 140ms for short prompts; our main worry is cost and 95th percentile tail.
[02:30] Samira: understood. For the pilot we recommend two benchmark sets: 1) small chat/512-token average prompts — target 95th pct < 350ms, 2) bulk embedding/longer sequence batch throughput aiming for sustained 100 QPS across the pool with acceptable avg latency. We'll provide a benchmark harness.
[02:52] Michael: how do you define QPS here? Is that concurrent requests or token throughput?
[02:58] Samira: QPS is requests per second (shot-level). Token throughput is a separate metric; we'll capture both. Our harness can replay traces from your logs to approximate token distributions.
[03:12] Priyanka: acceptance criteria — security sign-off plus performance within 20% of our baseline for tail latencies and successful SSO provisioning, plus audit log validation. If those are met, we move to contract for dedicated capacity.
[03:28] Jordan: that's reasonable. Timeline thoughts?
[03:31] Michael: we want pilot done within 4 weeks — two weeks for integration + SSO, two weeks for load and acceptance testing.
[03:40] Jordan: we can do that. We'll start with a 3–5 day SSO/SCIM integration window if your team can provision a test tenant and sample user set.
[03:49] Aisha: can you walk through the SSO flow quickly and any gotchas?
[03:52] Samira: sure — typical SAML SP-initiated flow, we provide metadata XML and an ACS endpoint. For group mapping we'll use SCIM to populate groups. Common gotchas: clock skew, certificate rollover, and nameID format mismatches. Also if you need attributes beyond standard, we'll need to extend the mapping.
[04:17] Priyanka: and on KMS — we need customer-managed keys for data at rest. Does Redwood support external KMS?
[04:24] Jordan: yes we support customer KMS integrations in Private or Dedicated modes; for hosted we offer encryption key management options and bring-your-own-key via our KMS integrations. We'll include the KMS integration doc.
[04:34] Leo: for the benchmark shapes, I'll send a token-size distribution and a list of representative prompts.
[04:39] Aisha: we'll also provide a small dataset of anonymized queries and expected cardinality for concurrency.
[04:44] Samira: perfect. Regarding model variants: we can pin a model version for the pilot and also test a smaller quantized variant if you want to explore cost/perf tradeoffs. For tail latency, continuous batching behavior can affect 95th percentile depending on request distribution, so we'll simulate both bursty and steady-state traffic.
[05:05] Michael: do you support debug hooks or traces for the requests during the pilot? We need tracing to correlate latencies with request ids.
[05:13] Samira: yes, request ids and tracinghooks are available; we'll enable verbose traces for the pilot and share access to our trace console for the duration.
[05:23] Jordan: ok let's capture acceptance criteria explicitly here: 1) SOC 2 + ISO docs received and acknowledged; 2) SSO tested with Okta and provisioning via SCIM; 3) audit logs exported and validated for required fields; 4) performance: 95th < 350ms on 512-token class and sustain 100 QPS for bulk path; 5) integration checklist completed — once all five met, sign-off moves to dedicated capacity discussion.
[06:00] Priyanka: one more thing — retention and e-discovery. We may need 24 months retention for certain logs for compliance. Is that possible?
[06:07] Samira: auditable exports can be stored in your S3 or we can retain; 24 months is doable but may require add-on retention plan. We'll note that as an optional add-on and include cost estimates.
[06:20] Michael: what's the expected cost for a 4-week pilot in terms of reserved capacity or credits?
[06:24] Jordan: pilot pricing typically covers a small reserved pool for predictable throughput plus overage. We'll send a tailored quote after we know the expected qps and token mix. For planning assume a modest reserved pool to hit 100 QPS for the test window.
[06:38] Leo: who are we engaging for security review? Is there a single contact?
[06:42] Jordan: Jordan is AE (that's me) for commercial, Samira for technical. We'll loop in our security engineer Mia Lopez if Priyanka wants an SSO/security deep dive.
[06:54] Priyanka: yes please include Mia. Also we'll need to run a short pen test scope review — not a full pen test yet, but a design review for any exposed endpoints.
[07:03] Samira: happy to support design review; we can provide network diagrams and endpoint specs.
[07:10] Michael: all right, let's recap next steps — Jordan?
[07:12] Jordan: we'll send: 1) SOC2/ISO artifacts and security datasheet, 2) SSO/SAML metadata and SCIM mapping template, 3) benchmark harness and initial scripts, 4) pricing estimate placeholders. Samira will deliver the benchmark plan. Cobalt will provide sample logs, Okta tenant info, and confirm retention window.
[07:35] Priyanka: sounds good. We'll aim to have the Okta test tenant by Friday.
[07:40] Jordan: great. Any other questions?
[07:43] Aisha: none from me.
[07:44] Leo: no.
[07:45] Jordan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule the SSO test kickoff for early next week.
[07:52] End of recording.

Notes about transcription: some technical terms may be transcribed imprecisely (e.g., "K V cache" instead of KV cache, "SOC two"), speaker labels may be slightly off in places.
